Question Choices: Fill: A bus and a taxi follow $t = 3d + 7$ and $t - 7 = 3d$. How many solutions does the system have? (Type 0, 1, or Infinite)
Hints: Use equivalent line equations: identical lines, distinct parallel lines, or one intersection.
Solution: In standard form the first equation has coefficients (-3,1) and right side 7. Multiplying it by 1 gives coefficients (-3,1) and right side 7. The second has the same left side and right side 7. The constants agree: the same line, infinitely many solutions. Requested answer: Infinite.

Question Choices: Fill: A number is split into two parts. One part is 2 more than half the other. Their sum is 32. Find the larger part.
Solution: x is the other part and y the part described as half plus 2. Compare their sizes after solving. System: y=x/2+2; x+y=32. Isolate y: y=(1/2)x+(2). Substitute into the other equation: (1)x+(1)[(1/2)x+(2)]=32. Combine: (3/2)x=30, so x=20. Then y=(1/2)(20)+(2)=12. Check both equations: -1/2(20)+1(12)=2; 1(20)+1(12)=32. Requested answer: 20.

Question Choices: Fill: Two brothers have ages that sum to 26. In 2 years, the older will be twice the younger. How old is the older brother now?
Solution: x is the younger brother’s current age and y the older brother’s; advance BOTH ages 2 years. System: x+y=26; y+2=2 × (x+2). Isolate y: y=(-1)x+(26). Substitute into the other equation: (-2)x+(1)[(-1)x+(26)]=2. Combine: (-3)x=-24, so x=8. Then y=(-1)(8)+(26)=18. Check both equations: 1(8)+1(18)=26; -2(8)+1(18)=2. Requested answer: 18.

Question Choices: Fill: Running time is twice stretching time. Total exercise time is 36 minutes. How many minutes are spent running?
Solution: x is stretching minutes and y running minutes. System: y=2 × x; x+y=36. Isolate y: y=(2)x+(0). Substitute into the other equation: (1)x+(1)[(2)x+(0)]=36. Combine: (3)x=36, so x=12. Then y=(2)(12)+(0)=24. Check both equations: -2(12)+1(24)=0; 1(12)+1(24)=36. Requested answer: 24.

Question Choices: Fill: A pet shop has cats and dogs, 14 animals total. There are 4 more dogs than cats. How many dogs are there?
Solution: x is cats and y dogs. Dogs exceed cats by 4. System: x+y=14; y=x+4. Multiply equation 1 by 1 and equation 2 by -1, then add to cancel y: (2)x=10, so x=5. Substitute back to obtain y=9. Check both equations: 1(5)+1(9)=14; -1(5)+1(9)=4. Requested answer: 9.
